rounds.q: What % of the world's mammals, by weight, are wild animals?
rounds.why: Farmed poultry is about 71% of all bird weight. Wild birds are just 29%.
rounds.src: Our World in Data, from Bar-On et al., PNAS (2018)
rounds.fun: Only 5% of mammal weight is wild animals. The wild ones are a tiny, fierce club!

rounds.q: What % of the world's known species are insects?
rounds.why: At any moment, about 10 quintillion insects are alive on Earth.
rounds.fun: About 10 quintillion insects are alive right now. Bugs are basically running the show!

rounds.q: What % of Earth's species have scientists formally described?
rounds.why: In the ocean it's even fewer: about 91% of sea species still await a name.
rounds.fun: Only 14% of species have been described. Most are still waiting for a name tag!

rounds.q: How old was the oldest Greenland shark scientists have dated?
rounds.why: Greenland sharks don't reach adulthood until they're about 156 years old.
rounds.fun: Greenland sharks don't grow up until about 156. Talk about a long childhood!

rounds.q: How many months is an African elephant pregnant?
rounds.why: The Virginia opossum gives birth just 11 to 13 days after mating.
rounds.src: National Geographic; PMC review of mammal gestation
rounds.fun: Elephant moms wait 22 months. Opossum moms? Just 11 to 13 days. Big difference!
